note: Canonical taxonomy for the Fragile Context Atlas: the failure MODES that make ingested context risky, and the DOMAINS where companies already feed fragile context into RAG / chatbots / agent memory / enterprise search / workflow agents. Single source — architecture/fragile_context_atlas.json packs reference mode ids + domain ids from here; scripts/check_fragile_context_atlas.py enforces the lock-step. This file does NOT redefine freshness or fact lifecycle: the TIME/FRESHNESS modes carry a `volatility_class` from schemas/artifacts/FragilityMetadata.v1.schema.json, PRIVACY carries a `scope` from the watchtower scope enum, and held-out examples use the held-out subset of CanonicalFact.status. Reuse, never duplicate.

reuses.scope: Fragile Fact Watchtower scope enum (global_public|tenant_private|tenant_override|system_reference) — PRIVACY_FRAGILE / CUSTOMER_FRAGILE
reuses.fact_status: schemas/artifacts/CanonicalFact.v1.schema.json status enum — held-out examples use {stale,contested,superseded,held_out,deprecated}; served answers map to verified_current/tenant_override
reuses.industry_vocab: vocabularies/industries.yaml — every domain.industry is a canonical industry id
reuses.quality_rubric: catalog/rubrics/baltor-fragile-information-quality.yaml — the audit-dimension layer (this taxonomy is the failure-mode + domain layer above it)
reuses.public_claim_policy: docs/sales/public-claim-and-engagement-policy.md — the atlas names system TYPES, never a vendor (enforced by the proof)

fragility_modes.label: Time-fragile
fragility_modes.definition: Correctness depends on a date, rate, fee, deadline, or effective period that changes over time.

fragility_modes.label: Authority-fragile
fragility_modes.definition: Truth depends on which source wins when a regulation / contract / system-of-record disagrees with an SOP, wiki, macro, or chat note.

fragility_modes.label: Jurisdiction-fragile
fragility_modes.definition: The correct answer varies by country, state, market, or regulatory regime.

fragility_modes.label: Customer-fragile
fragility_modes.definition: The answer varies by customer, tenant, product tier, or negotiated terms.

fragility_modes.label: Source-fragile
fragility_modes.definition: An informal source (blog, wiki, chat note, draft) competes with an official source of record.

fragility_modes.label: Conflict-fragile
fragility_modes.definition: Two or more sources disagree and the conflict must be surfaced, not silently averaged away.

fragility_modes.label: Action-fragile
fragility_modes.definition: The answer can trigger a payment, shipment, denial, legal step, customer commitment, or escalation.

fragility_modes.label: Compliance-fragile
fragility_modes.definition: Regulated advice or disclosure (financial, medical, legal, employment, safety) where a wrong served answer is a regulatory exposure.

fragility_modes.label: Privacy-fragile
fragility_modes.definition: Tenant-private, customer-private, employee-private, or patient-private context that must not leak across scope.

fragility_modes.label: Model-fragile
fragility_modes.definition: An LLM-derived or extracted value that has not been independently verified. LLM output is candidate, not truth.

fragility_modes.label: Freshness-fragile
fragility_modes.definition: Context decays and needs scheduled re-verification; freshness is not the same as correctness.
